headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust pathways exist; prompt injection and cascading errors are plausible, while compliance risk is limited by missing residency details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and uses uploaded knowledge base files, while mem0 is a memory layer likely to consume upstream outputs. A shared Dify server datastore plus file-based handoff creates a plausible injection path if mem0 ingests Dify-produced content as instructions. The exact bridge is undocumented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF mem0 ingests Dify-generated text as trusted memory or instructions
IF both agents exchange content through the shared Dify datastore or uploaded files
mitigations: Add a strict content-delimiter and instruction/data separator in the handoff
Strip tool directives from any text passed from Dify to mem0
Review one sample payload for prompt-injection markers
Disable automatic memory writes for untrusted sources
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify explicitly touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, and can write/read files; mem0 is a knowledge-management component with no egress, but it may still receive sensitive upstream context. Shared workspace or datastore exposure can leak sensitive data into mem0 outputs or persistence. Because residency and access controls are undocumented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Dify stores conversation logs or knowledge-base content that include secrets
IF mem0 persists or re-emits that content through shared state or downstream retrieval
mitigations: Remove secrets from any shared knowledge base before syncing
Limit Dify uploads to non-sensitive documents
Verify mem0 storage scope for one test record
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and encryption boundaries

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and network egress; mem0 has no network egress but its write/read surfaces are unspecified. The pair can still conflict over shared mutable state in Dify’s datastore or files even without explicit mem0 write permissions. Uncertainty about mem0’s write scope escalates this from low to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same Dify-managed workspace or datastore
IF mem0 has any hidden or external write path not shown in the profile
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Check for file-locking or optimistic concurrency support
Avoid shared mutable git or DB state
requires-engineering: add explicit locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify can generate workflow outputs from tools and files, and mem0 is a memory system that may treat upstream text as durable context. If mem0 accepts Dify output without verification, errors can propagate across sessions and be repeatedly reused. Because no verification boundary is documented, the interaction is plausibly medium rather than low.
conditions: IF mem0 stores Dify outputs as authoritative memory
IF downstream workflows act on that memory without human or programmatic verification
mitigations: Add a verification step before memory writes
Mark Dify outputs as untrusted until checked
Sample one end-to-end trace for hallucinated facts
Require citations for any stored claim
requires-engineering: implement confidence scoring and rejection rules

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and secrets, while mem0 is a memory store with no stated residency, retention, or subject-rights controls. That mismatch can create retention or deletion gaps for the same data class. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the pairwise flow, not either system alone.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify and then persisted in mem0
IF deletion or export requests must be honored across both systems
mitigations: Inventory which regulated data classes enter the pair
Check retention settings in both systems
Delete one test record end-to-end
Document a subject-rights workflow
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
